# Full-Stack Engineer (TypeScript / React) – Patient Experience

**Company:** Verdane Care (FICTIONAL)
**Location:** Graz, Austria (hybrid) or fully remote within Austria, Germany, Croatia or Slovenia
**Employment:** Full-time, permanent (or B2B contract in Croatia on request)
**Team:** Patient Experience squad (4 engineers, 1 designer, 1 product manager)

## About the role

Verdane Care makes appointment-booking and follow-up software for private clinics and physiotherapy practices. Patients use our web app and mobile web experience to book visits, fill in intake forms, receive reminders and view exercise plans.

As a Full-Stack Engineer you will build and improve those patient-facing features end to end – from React components and accessibility to the Node.js APIs and the database behind them. You will work in a small squad with a designer and a product manager, and you will ship to production several times a week.

## What you will do

- Build new patient-facing features in React and TypeScript, with a strong focus on accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) and performance on low-end phones
- Implement Node.js (NestJS) APIs and PostgreSQL schemas to support those features
- Integrate with third-party systems such as clinic calendars, SMS providers and payment gateways
- Write unit, integration and end-to-end tests (Jest, Playwright) and keep the build green
- Take part in design reviews, usability sessions and sprint planning
- Handle personal health data responsibly: follow our GDPR and data-minimisation guidelines, support audit requests from clinic customers
- Mentor interns or junior colleagues when the opportunity arises

## What you bring

**Must have**
- 2+ years of professional experience building web applications with React and TypeScript
- Experience writing backend services in Node.js (Express, NestJS or similar) and working with SQL databases
- Understanding of semantic HTML, responsive layouts and web accessibility basics
- Experience with automated testing (unit and end-to-end) and Git-based workflows
- Awareness of web security fundamentals (authentication, OWASP Top 10) and willingness to learn the privacy requirements of health data
- Fluent English; German or Croatian is helpful for customer-facing conversations

**Nice to have**
- Experience with Next.js or other server-side rendering frameworks
- Experience in healthcare, wellness or other regulated environments
- Familiarity with AWS or a similar cloud, and with Docker
- Experience with design systems and Storybook
- Experience with analytics and A/B testing

## What we offer

- Salary range EUR 54,000 – 70,000 gross per year depending on experience (Austrian collective agreement minimum applies)
- 25 days of holiday plus the Austrian public holidays, 5 additional well-being days and a EUR 1,200 yearly education budget
- Flexible hours, a home-office stipend and a yearly team retreat
- A friendly, low-ego team that cares about the people who use our software

## How to apply

Send your CV. A short cover letter and a link to something you have built (a portfolio, a GitHub project or a live site) are welcome but optional. We reply within ten working days.

Verdane Care is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace and welcomes applications from career changers and people returning to work.

company_info.company_description:
Verdane Care is a healthcare software company founded in Graz in 2019 by a physiotherapist and a software engineer. Its tools help private clinics, physiotherapy practices and dental offices simplify patient administration and care: Verdane Book supports online appointments and reminders, Verdane Intake digitises forms and consent, and Verdane Move provides physiotherapy exercise plans and follow-ups. More than 1,900 practices across Austria, Germany, Croatia and Slovenia use its products.

The company’s guiding principles are **“Patients first,” “Privacy by default” and “Simple beats clever.”** It takes data protection seriously, with ISO 27001 certification and patient data hosted exclusively in EU data centres. Accessibility is also a clear priority: its applications are built to WCAG 2.2 AA, with regular independent audits.

Verdane has 68 employees across Graz and Ljubljana, alongside remote colleagues. Its working environment includes engineering collaboration such as pair programming on request and weekly product demos with clinic staff—keeping teams close to the people who use their software. The company is growing its engineering and product teams, with an emphasis on building accessible, human-centred technology for healthcare.

## Verdane Care launches redesigned patient app and opens engineering hub in Ljubljana
**Graz, 22 September 2026**

Verdane Care, the Graz-based provider of appointment-booking software for private clinics, has launched a completely redesigned patient experience built on a new React-based design system. The new app cuts the median booking time from 94 to 41 seconds and passes the WCAG 2.2 AA audit commissioned from an independent accessibility consultancy.

The company also opened a small engineering hub in Ljubljana, Croatia, to recruit developers who prefer working in the Adriatic time zone. "Great engineers do not all live in Graz," said co-founder and CTO Jure Kovač. "We are hiring full-stack engineers who care about accessibility and about the people who will use the software."

Co-founder and CEO Dr. Lena Moser announced that Verdane will release a public developer API for clinic software vendors in spring 2027. The company says all patient data remains in EU data centres and that Verdane was recently re-certified under ISO 27001 without findings.

Verdane employs 68 people and plans to hire eight engineers, two designers and one data protection specialist before mid-2027.
# Careers at Verdane Care
*(fictional careers page – verdanecare.example/careers)*

## Join us and make healthcare feel human

**Engineering at Verdane**
- Front end: React, TypeScript, Next.js (marketing and clinic web), Storybook design system, Playwright
- Back end: Node.js (NestJS), PostgreSQL, Redis; AWS (Frankfurt region), Docker, GitHub Actions
- Practices: pair programming on request, weekly demos with real clinic staff, accessibility checks in CI, quarterly security reviews

cover_letter_history.content:
COVER LETTER

Dear Verdane Care Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Full-Stack Engineer role on the Patient Experience team. I am a computing graduate with hands-on experience building React applications, improving accessibility, creating reusable components and writing automated unit tests. Verdane Care’s focus on accessible, human-centred healthcare software makes this role especially compelling to me.

During my internship with Harbourline Media, I contributed to a React news site and resolved accessibility audit findings across more than 20 components, including keyboard navigation, colour contrast and ARIA labels. I also built a reusable image gallery, documented it with Storybook stories, and wrote tests with Jest and React Testing Library. More recently, I built a booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js and Tailwind CSS. These experiences align with the role’s emphasis on accessible patient-facing features and reliable web experiences.

My technical foundation also includes TypeScript, Node.js, Express and PostgreSQL, supported by my Tidewatch final-year project, which used React, TypeScript and Node.js. For my final-year project, I built Tidewatch, an accessible tide and weather app for sea swimmers using React, TypeScript and Node.js. I am drawn to Verdane Care’s principles of “Patients first,” “Privacy by default” and “Simple beats clever,” and to the opportunity to contribute to products that help patients manage appointments, forms and follow-up care.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my React and TypeScript experience, accessibility work, testing experience and technical foundation could contribute to Verdane Care’s Patient Experience team.

Kind regards,
Aiyana Brooks-Tan

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, and well targeted to Verdane Care’s Patient Experience team. It uses relevant evidence from the internship, freelance project, and Tidewatch project rather than relying only on generic claims. The accessibility example is particularly strong because it includes concrete scope: more than 20 components, keyboard navigation, colour contrast, and ARIA labels. The main content weakness is repetition: Tidewatch is mentioned twice in consecutive sentences. The letter also lists a technical foundation without clearly distinguishing demonstrated project experience from skills listed in the CV. It would be stronger with a more direct closing and slightly clearer evidence of Git-based workflows, wellness relevance, and the candidate’s fit for end-to-end development.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly in plain text and contains useful terms including React, TypeScript, Next.js, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, accessibility, ARIA labels, Storybook, Jest, React Testing Library, and Tailwind CSS. Its structure is easy to parse. However, it does not include several supported or relevant terms from the candidate material, especially Git/GitHub, WCAG 2.1, and the wellness context of the yoga booking website. It also does not explicitly address semantic HTML, responsive layouts, SQL databases, or privacy learning, although the candidate material does not provide enough evidence for all of these. AI screening probability is moderate to good for frontend/accessibility/testing keywords, but weaker for the full-stack and must-have requirements because the letter does not establish two years of professional experience, backend-service implementation, end-to-end testing, or security experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with the role’s frontend, accessibility, testing, Next.js, Storybook, and human-centred product aspects. Referencing “Patients first,” “Privacy by default,” and “Simple beats clever” is appropriately tailored to the company, and the accessible Tidewatch project plus yoga booking site provide relevant adjacent experience. The candidate’s material shows important gaps against the advertised profile: it does not establish 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience; it does not document writing Node.js backend services or end-to-end tests; and it does not show web-security fundamentals, authentication, OWASP Top 10, health-data privacy knowledge, AWS, Docker, analytics, or A/B testing. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than defects that can be fixed by rewriting. The letter should nevertheless present the supported evidence more precisely and avoid implying a stronger backend or full-stack track record than the material confirms.
